\begin{frame}[fragile]{Move sources are verified as VSL}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \textbf{Move} \hfill {\scriptsize\texttt{account.move}}
\begin{MoveSmall}
public entry fun deposit(addr: address,
                         amount: u64) {
  let value = &mut Balance[addr].balance.value;
  *value = *value + amount;
}
spec deposit {
  requires exists<Balance>(addr);
  modifies global<Balance>(addr);
  ensures Balance[addr].balance.value
    == old(Balance[addr].balance.value) + amount;
  aborts_if Balance[addr].balance.value
    + amount > MAX_U64;
}
\end{MoveSmall}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.53\textwidth}
      \textbf{VSL}, rendered from Move
\begin{LeanSmall}
module 0x42::account where
  public entry fun deposit(addr : Address,
      amount : u64) -> Unit := do
    let value := &mut Balance[addr].balance.value
    *value := *value + amount

  spec deposit where
    requires exists<Balance>(addr)
    ensures global<Balance>(addr).balance.value
      == old(global<Balance>(addr).balance.value)
         + amount
    aborts_if global<Balance>(addr).balance.value
      + amount > MAX_U64
    modifies global<Balance>(addr)
\end{LeanSmall}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \takeaway{One verifier for every source language: Move and Rust are rendered as VSL, and messages are mapped back to the original files.}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}[fragile]{Rust sources are verified as VSL}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \textbf{Rust} \hfill {\scriptsize\texttt{bounds.rs}}
\begin{RustSmall}
pub fn max(left: u32, right: u32) -> u32 {
    if left >= right { left } else { right }
}

pub fn raise(slot: &mut u32, floor: u32) {
    if *slot < floor {
        *slot = floor;
    }
}
\end{RustSmall}
      \textbf{VSL specifications} \hfill {\scriptsize\texttt{bounds.spec.lean}}
\begin{LeanSmall}
spec max where
  ensures result >= left && result >= right
  ensures result == left || result == right

spec raise where
  ensures slot >= floor
  ensures slot == old(slot) || slot == floor
\end{LeanSmall}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.53\textwidth}
      \textbf{VSL}, rendered from Rust
\begin{LeanSmall}
namespace bounds where
  fun max(left : u32, right : u32) -> u32 :=
    if left >= right then left else right

  spec max where
    ensures result >= left && result >= right
    ensures result == left || result == right

  fun raise(slot : &mut u32,
      floor : u32) -> Unit := do
    if *slot < floor then *slot := floor

  spec raise where
    ensures slot >= floor
    ensures slot == old(slot) || slot == floor
\end{LeanSmall}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[fragile]{From the Move developer's view}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
\begin{ShellSmall}
$ move prove --lean --package-dir vault
\end{ShellSmall}
{\scriptsize Messages at their Move source positions:}
\begin{ShellSmall}
vault.move:38:9: error: the specification
  clause `ensures result == ...` is not
  established
vault.move:61:13: error: the loop invariant
  `i < periods` is not preserved by an
  iteration
\end{ShellSmall}
      \begin{itemize}\small
        \item Also |aptos move prove --lean| and the Move Prover unit tests (|MVP_TEST_FEATURE=lean|).
        \item Budget per function in heartbeats: |pragma heartbeats|.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      When automation does not finish, the proof goes in a file beside the source:
\begin{MoveSmall}
spec square_of_sum {
  pragma verify = manual; // in proofs.proof.lean
  ensures result == a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b;
}
\end{MoveSmall}
\begin{LeanSmall}
-- proofs.proof.lean
verify square_of_sum by
  verex_obligations
  all_goals (first | verex_decide
    | (verex_prepare; all_goals try verex_decide))
  case ensures_1 =>
    rw [Int.add_mul, Int.mul_add, ...]
    omega
\end{LeanSmall}
      {\scriptsize |verify f by verex_obligations| lists the obligations, one |case| per clause.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[fragile]{The Solver Tactics}
  \begin{columns}[c]
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \centering
      \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
      \begin{tikzpicture}[font=\scriptsize, x=1cm, y=1cm,
          sstep/.style={proc, minimum width=4.4cm, minimum height=5.5mm, inner sep=2pt},
          split/.style={proc, fill=white, minimum width=1.35cm, minimum height=9mm, inner sep=2pt}]
        \node[art, minimum width=4.4cm] (g) at (0,3.3) {wp goal, split by \texttt{verex\_obligations}};
        \node[split] (lp) at (-1.5,2.2) {loops\\invariants};
        \node[split] (cl) at (0,2.2) {calls\\theorems};
        \node[split] (lf) at (1.5,2.2) {leaves};
        \node[sstep] (s1) at (0,1.05) {assumptions, memory and stored reads};
        \node[sstep] (s2) at (0,0.35) {frames, data and module invariants};
        \node[sstep] (s3) at (0,-0.35) {instances and witnesses};
        \node[sstep] (s4) at (0,-1.05) {\texttt{omega}, \texttt{decide}, \texttt{bv\_decide}};
        \node[sstep] (s5) at (0,-1.75) {\texttt{grind}, under a heartbeat budget};
        \node[art, draw=black!60, minimum width=4.4cm] (left) at (0,-2.75) {residual leaves (\texttt{ensures\_2}, \ldots): message, authored proof};
        \draw[arr] (g) -- (lp); \draw[arr] (g) -- (cl); \draw[arr] (g) -- (lf);
        \draw[arr] (lp) -- (lp |- s1.north);
        \draw[arr] (cl) -- (s1);
        \draw[arr] (lf) -- (lf |- s1.north);
        \draw[arr] (s1) -- (s2); \draw[arr] (s2) -- (s3); \draw[arr] (s3) -- (s4); \draw[arr] (s4) -- (s5);
        \draw[arr] (s5) -- (left);
        \begin{scope}[on background layer]
          \node[group, inner sep=2pt, fit=(s1)(s2)(s3)] (prep) {};
          \node[group, inner sep=2pt, fit=(s4)] (dec) {};
          \node[group, inner sep=2pt, fit=(s1)(s5), inner xsep=5pt] (solve) {};
        \end{scope}
        \node[font=\tiny\ttfamily, mNavy, anchor=east] at (prep.west) {verex\_prepare};
        \node[font=\tiny\ttfamily, mNavy, anchor=east] at (dec.west) {verex\_decide};
        \node[font=\tiny\ttfamily, mNavy, anchor=south east] at (solve.north west) {verex\_solve};
      \end{tikzpicture}%
      }
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.56\textwidth}
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}\small
        \item \textbf{Loops}: invariant at entry, preserved by an iteration, then the exit.
        \item \textbf{Calls}, as in the Move Prover: inlined unless native, opaque, or on a cycle; those go through contracts and theorems.
        \item \textbf{Leaves}, one per clause and path: |verex_prepare| normalizes, |verex_decide| runs the bounded deciders, |verex_solve| the full cascade, each under a budget.
        \item \textbf{Authored proofs}: Move |spec lemma| and |proof| blocks, or |verify f by| with the same tactics per clause (|case ensures_1 => ...|), then any Lean tactic.
        \item The solver is Lean meta code and \emph{untrusted}; only its proof terms are checked.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}[fragile]{What is proved, and what is trusted}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.56\textwidth}
\begin{LeanSmall}
theorem deposit.verified
    (prepared : prepareExecution registry unit
                  = .ok executable)
    (globalsPreserved : GlobalsPreserved executable) :
    SatisfiesFunction executable deposit
      deposit.contract
\end{LeanSmall}
      \scriptsize
      |SatisfiesFunction| reads the function's meaning off the big-step judgment.
      For every input meeting |requires|:
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
        \item every return meets |ensures| and the frame,
        \item every abort is one of |aborts_if|,
        \item no run is undefined.
      \end{itemize}
      Also:
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}
        \item partial correctness. 
        \item generic functions: proved once at a fresh type (monomorphization as in the Move Prover), valid at every instantiation.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \textbf{Trusted}
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\scriptsize
        \item Lean kernel, plus native |bv_decide| certificates.
        \item Big-step semantics of \LIR as the meaning of Move/Rust.
        \item Frontend (AST $\to$ \LIR) and contract translation.
      \end{itemize}
      \textbf{Not claimed}
      \begin{itemize}\scriptsize
        \item Anything about emitted bytecode; only up to stackless BC
      \end{itemize}
      \textbf{Proofs TBD}
      \begin{itemize}\scriptsize
        \item General agreement theorem, stated once over the compiler for every function.
        \item GlobalsPreserved: hypothesis, to be derived from type preservation.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
\begin{frame}[fragile]{The Verex Prover and the Move Prover}
  \small
  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
  \begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.17\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.37\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.4\textwidth}@{}}
    & \textbf{Move Prover} & \textbf{Verex Prover} \\
    \hline
    Input & bytecode after the compiler & checked AST $\to$ validated \LIR \\
    Engine & Boogie, Z3 / CVC5 & Lean tactics, Lean kernel \\
    Result & verdict, counterexample & theorem \\
    Semantics & implicit in the encoding & explicit big-step semantics, interpreter proved sound and complete \\
    References & reference elimination & prophecies (RustHorn) \\
    When stuck & timeout; restate the spec & message per clause; proof in |foo.proof.lean| \\
    Specifications & MSL & the same MSL, plus |pragma heartbeats| and |verify = manual| \\
  \end{tabular}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[fragile]{Status and next steps}
  \begin{columns}[T]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{Works today}
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\small
        \item |move prove --lean| on packages; Move Prover unit tests run with the Verex Prover.
        \item Nightly benchmark of 32 problems from |move-stdlib|, |aptos-stdlib|, the framework, Rust: 24 verify completely.
        \item Generics, storage, loops, vectors, function values, invariants, lemmas, state labels (in part).
        \item compiler-v2 compiles VSL; MonoVM differential tests.
        \item Rust, early: safe code from MIR, |verex-rust verify| with specifications in |foo.spec.lean|.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \textbf{Open}
      \begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\small
        \item Prove the agreement theorem; remove the last project axioms.
        \item Speed: the standard libraries in minutes.
        \item Coverage: intrinsic maps, remaining state labels, natives.
        \item Compiler correctness, VSL to bytecode.
        \item Rust: regions, drops and panics, unsafe code, library models.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\appendix
\talkframetitle

\begin{frame}[fragile]{Backup: \LIR and semantic profiles}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \LIR is language-neutral: functions carry a profile (Move, Rust).
    \item Profiles plug in twice:
      \begin{itemize}
        \item validation: which types, operations, intrinsics, and storage a profile admits;
        \item execution: how operations evaluate, what aborts or panics (Move abort codes, Rust |panic=abort|).
      \end{itemize}
    \item The same semantics is run by the interpreter, defined by the big-step relation, and used by the verifier.
    \item Validated namespaces are relocatable: modules link into units without re-validation.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup: references as prophecies}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item A mutable reference denotes a pair: the current value and a \emph{prophecy} of its final value (RustHorn).
    \item When the loan ends, the prophecy is resolved to the value then held.
    \item Validation computes where loans die; the interpreter, big-step relation, and verifier share this model.
    \item No heap or separation logic: Move's alias-free references and per-resource memory make this enough, also for Rust's safe subset.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
